```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(shokenuse)
```

The Sessions tab summarises each Claude Code session. It is the fastest way to find the one session that cost more than the rest.

## Value boxes

| Box | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Sessions | Number of sessions. |
| Median cost / session | Half of the sessions cost less than this. |
| Most expensive | Cost of the most expensive session. |
| Outliers | Sessions costing more than the mean plus two standard deviations. |

## Chart and table

The chart shows the 30 most expensive sessions. Each bar is labeled with the first 8 characters of the session id and the project. Outliers are orange.

The table has one row per session:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Session | Full session id. `claude --resume <session>` reopens it. |
| Project | Project, or a comma separated list when the session moved between projects. |
| Start | Time of the first prompt. |
| Minutes | Time from the first to the last prompt. A resumed session can span days. |
| Prompts, Tokens, Cost | Totals for the session. |
| First prompt | Text of the first prompt. |

Export CSV downloads the full table.

The code below builds the same table, draws the chart, and keeps only the outliers:

```{r}
#| label: sessions
sessions <- util_summarise_sessions(util_read_token_metrics())
util_plot_sessions(sessions)
dplyr::filter(sessions, outlier)
```
